texts.preamble: Ameer K.P vs Managing Director on 14 June, 2013 Author: K.Surendra Mohan Bench: K.Surendra Mohan In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr.Justice K.Surendra Mohan Monday,The 31St Day Of March 2014/10Th Chaithra, 1936 WP(C).No. 8447 of 2014 (E) --------------------------- Petitioner(S): -------------------------- Ameer K.P, Aged 33 Years S/O Kunjumuhammed, Kundupunathu House, Panoor P.O Thalassery, Kannur By Advs.Sri.K.S.Rajeev (Aluva) Smt.Dhanya Mohan Respondent(S): ---------------------------- 1. Exhibit R3(C): True Copy Of The Complaint Received By The Third Respondent On 31.07.2013 From K.J.Xavier, Head Vehicle Supervisor Exhibit R3(D): True Copy Of The Report Dated 10.08.2013 Submitted By P.G.Mohanan, General Controlling Inspector Of Aluva Unit Exhibit R3(E): True Copy Of The Notice Dated 14.08.2013 Issued By The Predecessor In Office Of The Third Respondent To The Petitioner Exhibit R3(F): True Copy Of The Report Dated 10.02.2014 Submitted By The Third Respondent To The Chief Traffic Officer, Ksrtc, Thiruvananthapuram Ameer K.P vs Managing Director on 14 June, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25346594/ 2 // True Copy // Pa To Judge K.Surendra Mohan, J. --------------------------------------------- W.P.(C) No.8447 of 2014 ---------------------------------------------- Dated this the 31st day of March, 2014 J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner is the licensee of a canteen and light refreshment stall at the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation Bus stand at Aluva. He has been conducting the said canteen and stall pursuant to a licence issued by the first respondent. As per Exhibit P1, his licence was renewed for a period of one year from 01.04.2013 to 31.03.2014. Therefore, the term of his licence expires today. According to the petitioner, the licence used to be renewed on the previous occasions, on the licensee remitting licence fee at a rate 10% in excess of the license fee of the previous year. It is contended that, Exhibit P5 is the memorandum that containss the terms and conditions subject to which the licence was granted. The petitioner has remitted the license fee for the entire period. Exhibit R3(c) is a complaint made by the Head Vehicle Supervisor, Aluva on 31.07.2013 complaining of an incident where a piece of glass was found in the food that he was consuming. He has stated in his complaint that, had he swallowed the piece of glass, the consequence would have been disastrous. On Exhibit R3(c), an enquiry had been ordered and according to the counsel for the respondents, the complaint was found to be true and the petitioner had been fined. The report is Exhibit R3(d), by which a fine of 500/- was imposed on the petitioner.
texts.arguments: He also has been issued with the requisite licencee under the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, which is valid up to 31.03.2014. The petitioner has been conducting the canteen for the past six years. According to him, there has been no cause for any complaint against the establishment from anyone, till date. However, in spite of the above by Exhibit P4, the petitioner has been informed that the licence in respect of the canteen could not be renewed in his favour for the period after 31.03.2014. The petitioner has filed this writ petition aggrieved by Exhibit P4. 2. According to the counsel for the petitioner, the petitioner has a vested right that has been recognized by Clause-3 of Exhibit R3(a), which according to the respondents is the memorandum that governs the transaction. Therefore, the petitioner has a right to insist that the licence be renewed in his favour provided he pays license fee at a rate 10% in excess of the rate for the previous year. The petitioner is willing to do so. Therefore, it is contended that the refusal to renew his licence is without any justification. The petitioner also alleges that, at the instance of the office bearers of recognized trade unions of the employees, unreasonable demands for money had been made, which the petitioner had refused to satisfy, thereby antagonizing them. Exhibit P4 has been issued, at their instance, it is contended. 3. Advocate Babu Joseph Kuruvathazha appears for the respondents. A counter affidavit has been filed by the third respondent. According to the counsel, Clause-3 of Exhibit R3(a) stipulates the submission of an application seeking renewal of the licence, two months before the date of expiry of the term of licence. It is pointed out that the petitioner's application referred to in Exhibit P3 is Ameer K.P vs Managing Director on 14 June, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25346594/ 3 dated 04.03.2014. So, the said application was not submitted within the time stipulated by the Clause. It is therefore contended that the petitioner is not entitled to claim the benefit of the said clause. Exhibit R3(b) is another application for renewal submitted by the petitioner, which is dated 12.02.2014. The said application is also not within the time stipulated by Clause-3. Therefore, in any view of the matter, it is submitted that the petitioner is not entitled to claim the benefit of the said clause. It is also contended that the petitioner has not satisfied the other conditions stipulated by the said clause. It is therefore contended that, the respondents are within their rights to refuse renewal of the license in respect of the canteen and no interference with the said proceedings is called for at the hands of this Court. 5. The counsel for the petitioner on the other hand points out that, Exhibit R3(c) complaint was made on 31.07.2013. Though allegations made in the complaint are serious warranting even criminal action against the petitioner, no such action has admittedly been initiated against him. Therefore, the counsel seeks the issue of Ameer K.P vs Managing Director on 14 June, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25346594/ 4 appropriate orders staying the conduct of the auction that is scheduled to be held on 02.04.2014. 6. Heard. It is not in dispute that, the petitioner is a licensee of the canteen and light refreshment stall. It is also not in dispute that the licence was being renewed from year to year. He has also not submitted his application for renewal within the time stipulated by the clause. 8. According to the counsel for the petitioner, clause 4 stipulates that persons who are not interested in renewing the license should inform the authorities regarding the said intention at least two months prior to the date of expiry of the period of licence. Since no such information had been communicated by the petitioner to the authorities, the only presumption that was available to the respondents was that the petitioner was desirous of continuing the stall for a further period.
